text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Kuwait's press on Monday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Kuwait rejects dancing parties in compliance with Islam, says official source. The conservative Moslem state bars public dancing parties in line with the teachings of Islam, but it allows concerts.
- State television, radio make $3.0 million from commercials in November, official says.
- Syria proposes tourism and industry projects for Kuwait investment.
- Notable decline in Kuwait Stock Exchange trade volume in the week to Wednesday.
- Saudi interior minister says kingdom has deported 400,000 illegal residents.

- Parliamentary panel to discuss television coverage of parliament's debates on Wednesday. Deputies say the state-run television's coverage of parliament avoids opposition criticism of government policies.
- Nurses at state hospitals to get 200 dinars ($667) pay rise a month.
- Virologist calms, says no polio in Kuwait.
- Kuwait, Lebanon, Egypt bourses to link up in 1997.
